blocking.problem: On Oracle and MongoDB, the D-A post-write identifier check reads only the first 5 000 rows (CHECK_BATCH) of the target and of the source, yet reports scope whole_table. A real identifier in any later row is never flagged, and the pack says passed with review_required false. Cause: key_floor (:218), _tally_target (:240) and the source loop of check_identifiers (:290) call rows.clear() on the page the connector yielded. oracle.py read_partition (:814-818) and mongo.py read_partition (:650-655) then test len() of that same, now empty, list and stop paging. PostgreSQL yields a fresh list (postgres.py:673) and is unaffected. Evidence: (1) 20 000-row synthesize packs: Oracle NATIONAL_ID and KYC DOC_NUMBER checked 5 000, MongoDB $.accounts[*].iban checked 5 000; the PostgreSQL control national_id checked 20 000. Round 2's packs show the same 5 000s. (2) Demo sources used as their own target: checked/in_source 5 000/5 000 against 19 998 expected; with pages copied, 20 000/19 998. (3) Scratch data, one shared ACCOUNT_NUMBER at target key 15 000 and source key 18 000: as built in_source 0 and review_columns [] on both engines; with pages copied, in_source 1 and review flagged. An append also gets a wrong key_floor. The unit test fake yields fresh lists, so it cannot catch this. Repros: ~/.cache/dps-build/reports/S1-M3-engines-r3/repro_idcheck_paging.py and repro_idcheck_missed_hit.py.
blocking.fix: Make paging independent of what the consumer does with a page. In oracle.py and mongo.py read_partition, compute the page length and the next after-key before yield, or yield a copy as postgres does. In identifier_check.py, stop clearing pages the connector owns. Add tests: (a) a conformance rule for all three engines that read_partition with a consumer clearing each page still returns every row; (b) check_identifiers on Oracle and on MongoDB with more rows than one page (or CHECK_BATCH patched small) and one shared value past page 1 gives in_source 1 and review; (c) key_floor is correct on a multi-page Oracle table; make the fake in tests/test_identifier_check.py alias its pages. Re-run a 20 000-row Oracle and MongoDB synthesize: checked must equal each column's non-null count. Note the fix in HANDOFF and M3-DEVIATIONS.

blocking.problem: R3-B1 (HIGH): the F-02 attack still freezes the whole server through /synthesize and /documents/synthesize. PrivacyEngine.synthesize (dps/engine/service.py:678-699) builds the detector and runs _detect synchronously inside the coroutine, so custom patterns and deny lists run on the event loop. transform.py:101 has no run_in_threadpool, and documents/__init__.py:398 has no to_thread. Since round 2, a run that leaves the 5 ms slice blocks the loop twice: first in MatcherPool._acquire (a Condition.wait with no timeout, queued behind other requests' runs), then in _Matcher._read for up to the 5 s ceiling. Measured on a real uvicorn server: /detect attack -> /health 0.00 s; /synthesize with the same body -> /health blocked 4.99 s; 6 /detect attacks then 1 /synthesize -> /health blocked 19.5 s; one client sending /synthesize back to back -> 26 of 29 one-second health checks failed. Round-1 code: 27/28 failed, so neither round fixed it. The regex_guard and pattern_process docstrings and review doc §3.2 claim the event loop stays free. No test covers synthesize.
blocking.fix: Run synthesize's synchronous engine work off the loop, as detect and obfuscate do: either asyncio.to_thread for the detector build, _detect and the transform inside PrivacyEngine.synthesize, or run the coroutine in the threadpool. Do the same in DocumentPipeline.run line 398 and for the detector builds in label_leftovers/label_templates. Make PatternBudget.run/MatcherPool.run refuse (fail closed, value-free) when the current thread runs an event loop. Add E2E tests: /health answers in under ~0.5 s during a /synthesize and a documents-synthesize stage-2 run (including when the pool is busy), and back-to-back synthesize attacks do not starve health checks. Correct the docstrings and §3.2.

blocking.problem: R3-B2 (MEDIUM, regression from round 2): building a deny-list trie (custom.compile_deny_list / deny_list_pattern) is outside every budget. It writes one character class per cased term character and compiles without IGNORECASE in regex's pure-Python parser, holding the GIL. The lru_cache(128) only helps repeated lists. The stage-2 child compiles the pattern again, also uncharged: its clock and RLIMIT start after compile. Measured: one /detect with 50 inline lists x 1000 random 50-char terms (2.70 MB body) costs 34.2 CPU-s (round-1 code: 3.4 s). The 7.2 MB variant costs 42.0 s (round 1: 9.2 s). Profile: 100% in compile_deny_list (2.47M regex parse_set calls). On /synthesize the build freezes the event loop: 0.59 s per new list. Review doc §3.2 ('compiled per term set once') and §5 ('never more than DPS_PATTERN_CPU_SECONDS', 'plus 5 ms GIL slices') are wrong, as is M5-DEVIATIONS ('never an unbounded build outside any budget').
blocking.fix: Bound and charge the build: charge each list's build thread-CPU to the call budget/ceiling and check left before building the next list. Cap the total deny-list characters per policy and the term length. Emit cheaper patterns (scoped (?i:) runs for plain-fold characters, explicit classes only for irregular ones such as the Turkish i's). Charge or limit the child's compile. Add a test with the 2.7 MB policy: it answers (200 or 422) within about the ceiling. Correct §3.2, §5, HANDOFF §6 and M5-DEVIATIONS.
